correctness.rationale: For f=X⁴+aX³+bX²+cX+d, the derivative coefficient structure yields total derivative-squarefree locus T=q²(q−1) in char 2 (a=0,c≠0) and q³(q−1) in odd characteristic (cubic derivative squarefree for p>3, b≠0 for p=3). In odd p a multiple root of f on the derivative-squarefree locus is exactly double. Prescribing a rational double root r makes f=(X−r)²g, g monic quadratic; checking f' separability contributes (q−1)² per r for p>3 and q(q−1) for p=3. Subtract double-counted q(q−1)/2 split double-root quartics; degree-2 gcd also includes (q²−q)/2 irreducible quadratic squares. These exhaustive cases yield precisely M1=q(q−1)(q−2) for p>3 or q(q−1)² for p=3, M2=q(q−1), and M0=T−M1−M2. In char2 M0=T, others 0. Since P(f squarefree)=1−1/q on all q⁴ monic quartics, and P(f_prime squarefree)=T/q⁴, arithmetic gives covariance 0 for p3 and (q−1)/q³ otherwise. An independent direct polynomial Euclidean-GCD enumerator checked q=2,3,4,5,7,9,11 incl extensions (7 field orders); matches all formulas. The unbounded prime-power theorem follows from counting, not sample extrapolation.
